The Challenge

A Narrow Audience and an Expensive Conversion

This client builds AI documentation software for medical specialists: it listens to patient visits, writes the clinical notes, and recommends billing codes. A strong product, but a brutal paid acquisition problem. The buyer is a narrow professional audience, the conversion event is a booked sales demo, and every wasted impression is expensive.

Early creative tests reflected that difficulty: demos were coming in at $250 to $310+ each, with no structured system for deciding which ads to kill and which to scale. At those costs, paid acquisition couldn't be a real growth channel.

The Strategy

A Creative Testing Engine, Not One-Off Ads

We rebuilt the account around a disciplined testing system. Every ad gets classified red, yellow, or green based on performance. Underperformers are cut inside a 12-14 day window, and proven winners keep running, with 9-10 winning ads live concurrently at any time. New creative enters the rotation on a fixed cadence instead of ad hoc.

On the targeting side, campaigns were segmented by medical specialty so messaging could speak directly to each audience's workflow. And instead of optimizing for clicks or cheap leads, we wired the booked-demo event into Meta through the Conversions API, so the algorithm optimized on the one action that actually matters to the business.

Red/Yellow/Green Rotation Specialty Targeting Conversions API Demo-Event Optimization Fixed Testing Cadence
The Results

From $250+ Per Demo to $59-89 in the Best Ad Sets

The flagship campaign has generated 417 booked demos at a $147.22 lifetime average, a figure that includes every early test along the way. By spring 2026, the optimized system was booking demos at $59 to $89 in its best ad sets, with a weighted account average around $134.

Across the account, we've delivered over 3.5 million impressions and managed $145,000+ in spend across 15 campaigns. The engagement is now in its 16th month, with monthly spend having scaled past $10,000.

FAQ

B2B SaaS Meta Ads: Common Questions

What is a good cost per booked demo for B2B SaaS Meta ads?

It depends heavily on the audience. In this engagement targeting medical specialists, unoptimized creative tests came in at $250-$310+ per booked demo, while the optimized system reached $59-$89 in the best ad sets with a weighted account average around $134. For narrow professional audiences, anything under $150 per demo is strong performance.

Do Meta ads work for B2B SaaS demo generation?

Yes, when the account optimizes on the right signal. This campaign generated 417 booked sales demos from cold Meta traffic by wiring the booked-demo event into Meta through the Conversions API, so the algorithm optimized for demos rather than clicks or cheap leads.

How long does it take to lower cost per booked demo on Meta?

With a disciplined testing cadence, meaningful improvement compounds over months, not days. This account used a red/yellow/green creative rotation with a 12-14 day cut window for underperformers. Over the engagement, cost per demo dropped from $250+ in early tests to $59-$89 in the best ad sets.

Should B2B SaaS companies optimize Meta ads for leads or demos?

Demos. Optimizing for form leads produces volume that rarely converts to pipeline for high-consideration B2B products. Passing the booked-demo event back to Meta via the Conversions API trains delivery on the action that actually generates revenue, which is what made this account scalable.
